source.text: בְּרֵאשִׁ֖ית בָּרָ֣א אֱלֹהִ֑ים אֵ֥ת הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם וְאֵ֥ת הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: In beginning created God the heavens and the earth.

en.L: In [the] beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
en.B: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
en.R: In the beginning, God created everything: the heavens and the earth.

es.L: En [el] principio creó Dios los cielos y la tierra.
es.B: En el principio Dios creó los cielos y la tierra.
es.R: En el principio, Dios creó todo: el cielo y la tierra.

fr.L: Au commencement Dieu créa les cieux et la terre.
fr.B: Au commencement, Dieu créa les cieux et la terre.
fr.R: Au tout début, Dieu a créé tout ce qui existe : le ciel et la terre.

sw.L: Mwanzoni Mungu aliumba mbingu na dunia.
sw.B: Mwanzoni, Mungu aliumba mbingu na dunia.
sw.R: Mwanzo kabisa, Mungu aliumba kila kitu: mbingu na dunia.

decisions.choice: In the beginning: a statement that stands on its own and opens the account
alternatives: When God began to create the heavens and the earth (a time clause that leads into verse 2 or 3)
decisions.reason: The word for beginning has no article, and the verse could be read as leading into what follows: "When God began to create the heavens and the earth, the earth was formless...". The second account opens in a similar way (2:4: "in the day that the LORD God made..."). But the Masoretic accents mark a pause after the first word, so that it reads as complete in itself, and the Septuagint, the oldest translation, reads the verse as a main clause, as John 1:1 echoes it. Read either way, God is there and acting before anything else is described.

decisions.choice: created: a verb that the Bible uses only with God as the one who acts
decisions.reason: In the Old Testament this verb is used only of what God does, and it never names a material that something is made from. Genesis 1 uses it at three points: for the heavens and the earth (verse 1), for the first living creatures (verse 21) and for human beings (verse 27, three times). The chapter also uses everyday verbs such as "made" for God's work, so this verb alone does not settle how God created; but the opening verse places God before and above everything that exists.

decisions.choice: God: the one God, though the word is plural in form
decisions.reason: The word is plural in form and in other places can mean "gods" (Exodus 20:3). Here its verb is singular, "he created", as it is throughout the chapter, so it names the one God. Hebrew often uses a plural form to express greatness or fullness.

decisions.choice: the heavens and the earth: everything that exists
alternatives: the sky and the land, and nothing more
decisions.reason: Naming two opposite ends to mean everything between them is a common way of speaking in Hebrew. "The heavens and the earth" is the whole ordered world, from the sky above to the ground below; Hebrew has no single word for the universe. The account closes with the same words (2:1).

decisions.choice: In [the] beginning
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no article here (meaning decision m1); English needs one, so Literal brackets it.

decisions.choice: everything: the heavens and the earth
decisions.reason: Readable says what the pair of words means (m4) and keeps the words themselves.

decisions.choice: creó Dios (L); Dios creó (B, R)
decisions.reason: Hebrew narrative puts the verb before its subject. Spanish allows the same order, and Literal keeps it through the chapter ("Y dijo Dios", "Y vio Dios"). Balanced and Readable put the subject first, the more usual order in modern Spanish narrative.

decisions.choice: el cielo y la tierra
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word for heavens is always plural, and Literal and Balanced keep the plural "los cielos". Readable uses the singular "el cielo", the everyday Spanish word; the pair still means everything that exists (m4).

decisions.choice: passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("créa", "dit", "vit"); passé composé at Readable ("a créé", "a dit")
decisions.reason: For the whole of Genesis, as the French style guide sets out: the passé simple is the normal tense of written French narrative and suits a careful public reading, while Readable uses the passé composé, the tense of spoken French and of school reading today. Speech inside the story keeps the tenses of speech at every level.

decisions.choice: les cieux (L, B); le ciel (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is plural in form, and Literal and Balanced keep the plural "les cieux", which French still uses for the heavens as a whole; Readable says "le ciel", the everyday word. "Au commencement" needs no bracket for the article, which is part of the contraction (style guide).

decisions.choice: mbingu na dunia
decisions.reason: "Dunia" is the whole earth, the sense here (m4); "nchi" is the land or a country. Swahili therefore says "dunia" in verses 1-2 and "nchi" from verse 9, where the same Hebrew word becomes the name of the dry land (verse 10), a link English keeps with "earth" and Swahili cannot.

source.text: וְהָאָ֗רֶץ הָיְתָ֥ה תֹ֨הוּ֙ וָבֹ֔הוּ וְחֹ֖שֶׁךְ עַל־פְּנֵ֣י תְה֑וֹם וְר֣וּחַ אֱלֹהִ֔ים מְרַחֶ֖פֶת עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הַמָּֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And the earth was formlessness and emptiness, and darkness [was] over [the] face of [the] deep, and [the] spirit of God [was] hovering over [the] face of the waters.

en.L: And the earth was formlessness and emptiness, and darkness [was] over the face of the deep, and the Spirit of God [was] hovering over the face of the waters.
en.B: The earth was without form and empty. Darkness lay over the surface of the deep, while the Spirit of God hovered above the waters.
en.R: The earth did not have any shape yet, and it was empty. It was dark over the deep water, and the Spirit of God was moving above the water.

es.L: Y la tierra era desolación y vacío, y [había] oscuridad sobre la faz del abismo, y el Espíritu de Dios [estaba] aleteando sobre la faz de las aguas.
es.B: La tierra estaba sin forma y vacía. La oscuridad cubría la superficie del abismo, mientras el Espíritu de Dios se cernía sobre las aguas.
es.R: La tierra todavía no tenía forma, y estaba vacía. Sobre las aguas profundas todo estaba oscuro, y el Espíritu de Dios se movía por encima del agua.

fr.L: Et la terre était désolation et vide, et l’obscurité [était] sur la face de l’abîme, et l’Esprit de Dieu voltigeait sur la face des eaux.
fr.B: La terre était sans forme et vide. L’obscurité recouvrait la surface de l’abîme, tandis que l’Esprit de Dieu planait au-dessus des eaux.
fr.R: La terre n’avait encore aucune forme, et elle était vide. Tout était sombre au-dessus des eaux profondes, et l’Esprit de Dieu se déplaçait au-dessus de l’eau.

sw.L: Na dunia ilikuwa bila umbo na tupu, na giza [lilikuwa] juu ya uso wa kilindi, na Roho wa Mungu [alikuwa] akielea juu ya uso wa maji.
sw.B: Dunia ilikuwa bila umbo na tupu. Giza lilitanda juu ya kilindi cha maji, na Roho wa Mungu alikuwa akielea juu ya maji.
sw.R: Dunia ilikuwa bado haina umbo lolote, na ilikuwa tupu. Juu ya maji yenye kina kirefu kulikuwa na giza, na Roho wa Mungu alikuwa akisonga juu ya maji.

decisions.choice: Now the earth was: a description of how things stood, not the next event
alternatives: And the earth became formless and empty (a ruin after an earlier creation)
decisions.reason: The verse puts "the earth" before its verb, a Hebrew way of pausing the story to describe a scene. It tells how things were when God first spoke in verse 3. The verb "was" describes a state here, as it does in 3:1 ("the serpent was more cunning"); it does not say that the earth became formless after an earlier creation.

decisions.choice: formless and empty: not yet ordered and not yet filled
decisions.reason: The two words rhyme in Hebrew. The first is used for a trackless wasteland (Deuteronomy 32:10) and for what is empty or useless; the second appears only with the first (Isaiah 34:11; Jeremiah 4:23, which looks back to this verse). The rest of the chapter answers both: on days one to three God gives the world its form, and on days four to six he fills it.

decisions.choice: the deep: the deep waters that covered the earth
decisions.reason: The word means the waters of the deep sea and the springs beneath the earth (7:11; Psalm 104:6). Here it is the water that covers everything before God separates the waters and the dry land appears (verses 6-10). In this account the deep is not a power that opposes God; it is water, waiting for his word.

decisions.choice: the Spirit of God
decisions.reason: The word means breath, wind or spirit. With "God" it could mean a very great wind, since Hebrew sometimes uses "of God" to mean "mighty", and God sends a wind over the waters after the flood (8:1). But elsewhere "the spirit of God" is God's own Spirit at work (Exodus 31:3; 1 Samuel 10:10), and the verb "hovering" (m5) suits a living presence better than a wind. Psalm 33:6 links God's word and his breath in the making of the heavens.

decisions.choice: hovering: moving above, as a bird does over its young
decisions.reason: The same rare verb describes an eagle hovering over its young in Deuteronomy 32:11. It pictures God's presence over the waters, ready to bring order and life.

decisions.choice: the face of (L); the surface of, then simply the waters (B); over the deep water (R)
alternatives: the face of the deep ... the face of the waters
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "face", the Hebrew way of saying "surface", both times. Balanced says "surface" once and lets "the waters" stand alone the second time; Readable says "deep water" for the deep.

decisions.choice: desolación y vacío (L); sin forma y vacía (B); no tenía forma ... estaba vacía (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the two nouns of the Hebrew: "desolación" for the empty waste the first word names elsewhere, "vacío" for the emptiness (m2). Balanced and Readable say what the pair means: not yet given form and not yet filled (m2). The traditional "desordenada" suggests a mess rather than a world not yet ordered; "informe" is literary; "caos" turns the pair into one word. Spanish cannot keep the rhyme of the Hebrew pair. A reviewer should check that "desolación" does not suggest a ruin after an earlier creation, a reading m1 sets aside.

decisions.choice: el abismo (L, B); las aguas profundas (R)
decisions.reason: "Abismo" is the established Spanish word for the deep and in ordinary use names the depths of the sea. Here it means the deep waters that covered the earth (m3), not a bottomless pit or a hostile power. Readable says "las aguas profundas" so that young readers see that it is water.

decisions.choice: oscuridad
decisions.reason: "Tinieblas" is the traditional Bible word but now sounds literary. "Oscuridad" is the ordinary word, used at every level here and in verses 4, 5 and 18.

decisions.choice: voltigeait (L); planait (B); se déplaçait (R)
decisions.reason: Literal uses "voltiger", the movement of a bird over its young, to keep the picture of Deuteronomy 32:11 (m5); Balanced says "planait", the natural French for hovering above; Readable says simply that the Spirit was moving above the water.

decisions.choice: l'obscurité
decisions.reason: "Les ténèbres" is the traditional word, but it is now literary and always plural. "L'obscurité" is the ordinary French for darkness and names the same thing at every level; it is used through this chapter.

decisions.choice: Roho wa Mungu ... alikuwa akielea (L, B); akisonga (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision (m4) reads this as God's own Spirit, so the noun takes the personal agreement used for the Holy Spirit in modern Swahili ("wa", "alikuwa") rather than the class agreement for wind or breath. "Kuelea" is to hover or float above; Readable says only that the Spirit was moving.

records.literal_gloss: And said God, let be light, and was light.

en.L: And God said, "Let there be light," and there was light.
en.B: God said, "Let there be light," and light came into being.
en.R: Then God said, "Let there be light!" And light began to shine.

es.L: Y dijo Dios: «Haya luz», y hubo luz.
es.B: Dios dijo: «Que haya luz», y la luz comenzó a existir.
es.R: Entonces Dios dijo: «¡Que haya luz!». Y la luz empezó a brillar.

fr.L: Et Dieu dit : « Qu’il y ait de la lumière », et il y eut de la lumière.
fr.B: Dieu dit : « Qu’il y ait de la lumière », et la lumière apparut.
fr.R: Puis Dieu a dit : « Qu’il y ait de la lumière ! » Et la lumière s’est mise à briller.

sw.L: Na Mungu akasema, "Kuwe na nuru," na kukawa na nuru.
sw.B: Mungu akasema, "Kuwe na nuru," nayo nuru ikatokea.
sw.R: Kisha Mungu akasema, "Nuru iwepo!" Nayo nuru ikaanza kung'aa.

decisions.choice: let there be ... and there was: the command and the result use the same verb
decisions.reason: God's command "let it be" and the report "and it was" are two forms of one verb, so the report repeats the command word for word. The pattern returns through the chapter: God speaks, and what he says happens (Psalm 33:9).

decisions.choice: light before the sun: light is made on the first day, the sun on the fourth
alternatives: the light of the sun, coming through for the first time
decisions.reason: The sun, moon and stars are not made until verses 14-19. The account presents light as God's first work, coming from his word, not from the lights in the sky; they are later given the task of carrying it. Later scripture speaks of God himself as light (Psalm 104:2; Isaiah 60:19), and Paul recalls this verse: "Let light shine out of darkness" (2 Corinthians 4:6).

decisions.choice: light came into being (B); light began to shine (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "and there was light", which repeats the command as the Hebrew does (m1). Balanced and Readable say what happened in a verb of their own.

decisions.choice: «Haya luz», y hubo luz
alternatives: «Sea la luz», y fue la luz
decisions.reason: One Spanish verb, "haber", gives both the command and the report, as one Hebrew verb does (m1). The traditional "Sea la luz ... y fue la luz" uses "ser", which in current Spanish no longer says that something comes into being.

decisions.choice: Qu'il y ait de la lumière ... il y eut de la lumière (L); la lumière apparut (B); s'est mise à briller (R)
alternatives: Que la lumière soit ... et la lumière fut
decisions.reason: Literal repeats the same verb in the command and in the report, as the Hebrew does (m1), and keeps light without an article, as the Hebrew has none. "Que la lumière soit" is the shape of the traditional French Bibles and is not followed; Balanced and Readable say what happened in a verb of their own, as the English does.

decisions.choice: Kuwe na nuru ... kukawa na nuru (L); nuru
decisions.reason: "Nuru" is the word for light as God's gift and as a figure (as in John); "mwanga" is everyday light. Literal says "let there be light ... and there was light" with the same existential verb in both halves, as the Hebrew repeats its verb (m1).

source.text: וַיַּ֧רְא אֱלֹהִ֛ים אֶת־הָא֖וֹר כִּי־ט֑וֹב וַיַּבְדֵּ֣ל אֱלֹהִ֔ים בֵּ֥ין הָא֖וֹר וּבֵ֥ין הַחֹֽשֶׁךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And saw God the light, that [it was] good, and separated God between the light and between the darkness.

en.L: And God saw the light, that [it was] good, and God separated between the light and the darkness.
en.B: God saw that the light was good, and God divided the light from the darkness.
en.R: God saw that the light was good. He divided the light from the darkness.

es.L: Y vio Dios la luz, que [era] buena, y separó Dios entre la luz y la oscuridad.
es.B: Dios vio que la luz era buena, y separó la luz de la oscuridad.
es.R: Dios vio que la luz era buena. Luego separó la luz de la oscuridad.

fr.L: Et Dieu vit la lumière, qu’[elle était] bonne, et Dieu sépara entre la lumière et l’obscurité.
fr.B: Dieu vit que la lumière était bonne, et Dieu sépara la lumière de l’obscurité.
fr.R: Dieu a vu que la lumière était bonne. Il a séparé la lumière de l’obscurité.

sw.L: Na Mungu akaiona nuru, kwamba [ni] njema, na Mungu akatenganisha kati ya nuru na giza.
sw.B: Mungu akaona kwamba nuru ni njema, akaitenganisha nuru na giza.
sw.R: Mungu akaona kwamba nuru ni njema. Akatenganisha nuru na giza.

decisions.choice: good: as it should be, fit for its purpose and pleasing to God
decisions.reason: The word covers what is pleasant, useful and right. Here it is God's verdict that what he has made is as it should be. The verdict comes seven times in the chapter, the last time "very good" (verse 31).

decisions.choice: separated: God divides one thing from another and so gives the world its order
decisions.reason: Separating is a key act of the first days: light from darkness, the waters above from the waters below (verse 7), day from night (verse 14). Each separation sets a boundary, and the boundaries make the world a place where life can live.

decisions.choice: saw the light, that [it was] good
alternatives: saw that the light was good
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew order, in which God sees the light and then judges it good, and brackets "it was", which Hebrew does not need.

source.text: וַיִּקְרָ֨א אֱלֹהִ֤ים׀לָאוֹר֙ י֔וֹם וְלַחֹ֖שֶׁךְ קָ֣רָא לָ֑יְלָה וַֽיְהִי־עֶ֥רֶב וַֽיְהִי־בֹ֖קֶר י֥וֹם אֶחָֽד׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And called God to the light day, and to the darkness he called night. And was evening and was morning, day one.

en.L: And God called the light Day, and the darkness {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called Night. And there was evening and there was morning, day one.
en.B: God named the light Day, and the darkness {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} named Night. Evening came, and then morning: the first day.
en.R: God gave the light the name Day, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave the darkness the name Night. Evening passed, and morning came. That was the first day.

es.L: Y llamó Dios a la luz Día, y a la oscuridad llamó Noche. Y hubo tarde y hubo mañana, día uno.
es.B: Dios dio a la luz el nombre de Día, y a la oscuridad, el de Noche. Llegó la tarde, y después la mañana: el primer día.
es.R: Dios le puso a la luz el nombre de Día, y a la oscuridad le puso el nombre de Noche. Pasó la tarde y llegó la mañana. Ese fue el primer día.

fr.L: Et Dieu appela la lumière Jour, et l’obscurité, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} l’appela Nuit. Et il y eut un soir et il y eut un matin, jour un.
fr.B: Dieu nomma la lumière Jour, et l’obscurité, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} la nomma Nuit. Le soir vint, puis le matin : le premier jour.
fr.R: Dieu a donné à la lumière le nom de Jour, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a donné à l’obscurité le nom de Nuit. Le soir est passé, puis le matin est venu. C’était le premier jour.

sw.L: Na Mungu akaiita nuru Mchana, na giza akaliita Usiku. Na kukawa jioni, na kukawa asubuhi, siku moja.
sw.B: Mungu akaipa nuru jina Mchana, na giza akalipa jina Usiku. Jioni ikaja, kisha asubuhi: siku ya kwanza.
sw.R: Mungu akaipa nuru jina la Mchana. Giza akalipa jina la Usiku. Jioni ikapita, asubuhi ikafika. Hiyo ilikuwa siku ya kwanza.

decisions.choice: called: naming as a sign of authority
decisions.reason: In the Bible the one who gives a name has authority over what is named. God names day and night, the sky (verse 8), and the land and the seas (verse 10); later he lets the man name the animals (2:19-20).

decisions.choice: day one: the first day, with a cardinal number
decisions.reason: Hebrew uses the number "one" here, though it uses "second", "third" and so on for the other days. "One" can stand for "first" when counting (2:11; 8:13), so the meaning is the first day. The day is counted from evening, as Israel's days were counted from sunset.

decisions.choice: day: the daylight, and then a whole day marked by evening and morning
decisions.reason: The word has two senses in this verse: the daylight that God names, as against night, and the whole day that evening and morning complete. Each of the six days of work is marked in the same way, and the seventh is the day God rests (2:2-3), the pattern Israel's week follows (Exodus 20:11). Readers differ on how these days relate to the age of the world; the text presents them as a week.

decisions.choice: named (B); gave ... the name (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "called the light Day". Balanced and Readable say "named", which is what calling means here (m1).

decisions.choice: day one (L); the first day (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew pattern "and there was ... and there was". Balanced and Readable say the same in a form that reads naturally aloud. Literal keeps the number "one" so the reader can see it; Balanced and Readable use the ordinal English expects (m2).

decisions.choice: la tarde
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is the evening, the close of daylight with which a new day began (m2). "La tarde" is the usual Spanish word for that time; "la noche" would blur it with the Night just named, and "el atardecer" is only the sunset itself.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}}
decisions.reason: For the whole book: every pronoun for God takes the deity pronoun setting, lowercase by default and capitalised as the alternative, as in the French New Testament (il, lui, le, l', son, sa, ses, and moi, me, mon, toi, te, tu, ton when God speaks or is spoken to, including an inverted "-tu"). "Je" has no span, and a pronoun that opens a sentence is written plainly with its capital ("Il a séparé", verse 4). French may need a span where English has none (an object "le", "lui") and the reverse.

decisions.choice: no span: akaliita, akalipa
decisions.reason: For the whole book: Swahili marks the subject "he" inside the verb, where no capital is possible, so the deity pronoun setting goes only on free pronouns for God (yeye, naye, mimi, nami, wewe, and the possessives wake, yake, wangu, yako...), even where the English has no span, as in Genesis 15:1. Here the English "he" has no Swahili counterpart, and Swahili therefore has fewer spans than English.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֔ים יְהִ֥י רָקִ֖יעַ בְּת֣וֹךְ הַמָּ֑יִם וִיהִ֣י מַבְדִּ֔יל בֵּ֥ין מַ֖יִם לָמָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said God, let be a vault in [the] midst of the waters, and let it be separating between waters to waters.

en.L: And God said, "Let there be a vault in the midst of the waters, and let it be separating between waters and waters."
en.B: God said, "Let there be a vault in the middle of the waters, to divide water from water."
en.R: Then God said, "Let there be a great dome in the middle of the waters. Let it keep the water below apart from the water above."

es.L: Y dijo Dios: «Haya una bóveda en medio de las aguas, y que esté separando entre aguas y aguas».
es.B: Dios dijo: «Que haya una bóveda en medio de las aguas, para separar unas aguas de otras».
es.R: Entonces Dios dijo: «Que haya una gran cúpula en medio de las aguas. Que separe el agua de abajo del agua de arriba».

fr.L: Et Dieu dit : « Qu’il y ait une voûte au milieu des eaux, et qu’elle fasse séparation entre eaux et eaux. »
fr.B: Dieu dit : « Qu’il y ait une voûte au milieu des eaux, pour que les eaux soient séparées les unes des autres. »
fr.R: Puis Dieu a dit : « Qu’il y ait un grand dôme au milieu des eaux. Qu’il sépare l’eau d’en bas de l’eau d’en haut. »

sw.L: Na Mungu akasema, "Kuwe na kuba katikati ya maji, nalo liwe likitenganisha kati ya maji na maji."
sw.B: Mungu akasema, "Kuwe na kuba katikati ya maji, ili liyatenganishe maji haya na maji yale."
sw.R: Kisha Mungu akasema, "Kuwe na kuba kubwa katikati ya maji. Liyatenganishe maji ya chini na maji ya juu."

decisions.choice: vault: a solid-looking expanse, beaten out like metal, that holds back the waters above
decisions.reason: The word comes from a verb for hammering metal into a thin sheet (Exodus 39:3), and Job 37:18 pictures the skies as hard as a mirror of cast metal. The vault is what we see as the sky: it holds back waters above it (verse 7), and the sun, moon and stars are set in it (verse 17). The account describes the world as it appears to someone standing on the earth.

decisions.choice: vault (L, B); great dome (R)
decisions.reason: "Firmament", from the Latin, is the old English word, but few readers know it now. "Expanse" loses the sense of something solid. "Vault", an arched ceiling, keeps both the shape and the solidity (m1); Readable uses "great dome", a plainer picture of the same thing.

decisions.choice: the water below apart from the water above
decisions.reason: Readable takes "below" and "above" from verse 7 to make clear which waters are meant.

decisions.choice: bóveda (L, B); gran cúpula (R)
decisions.reason: "Firmamento", the traditional word, is now heard as a poetic name for the sky and has lost the sense of something solid; "expansión" loses it too. "Bóveda", an arched ceiling, keeps both the shape and the solidity of the Hebrew picture (m1). Readable says "una gran cúpula", a dome, the plainer image of the same thing.

decisions.choice: une voûte (L, B); un grand dôme (R)
decisions.reason: As the English (r-en-1): "voûte", an arched ceiling, keeps both the shape and the solidity of the Hebrew picture (m1); "étendue" loses the solidity, and "firmament" is a word few readers know. Readable says "un grand dôme".

decisions.choice: kuba (L, B); kuba kubwa (R)
decisions.reason: "Anga" is the open sky or air and loses the solid vault of the Hebrew picture (m1); "kuba", a dome, keeps it, and "Anga" is kept for the name God gives the vault (verse 8). Taken here as a class 5 noun (kuba hilo, liyatenganishe); a native reviewer should confirm the word and its agreement.

source.text: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ אֱלֹהִים֮ אֶת־הָרָקִיעַ֒ וַיַּבְדֵּ֗ל בֵּ֤ין הַמַּ֨יִם֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ מִתַּ֣חַת לָרָקִ֔יעַ וּבֵ֣ין הַמַּ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֖ר מֵעַ֣ל לָרָקִ֑יעַ וַֽיְהִי־כֵֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And made God the vault, and separated between the waters which [were] from under to the vault and between the waters which [were] from above to the vault. And was so.

en.L: And God made the vault, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} separated between the waters that [were] under the vault and the waters that [were] above the vault. And it was so.
en.B: So God made the vault and divided the waters beneath it from the waters above it. And so it happened.
en.R: So God made the dome. He separated the water under the dome from the water above it. And that is what happened.

es.L: E hizo Dios la bóveda, y separó entre las aguas que [estaban] debajo de la bóveda y las aguas que [estaban] encima de la bóveda. Y fue así.
es.B: Así hizo Dios la bóveda, y separó las aguas que estaban debajo de ella de las aguas que estaban encima. Y así sucedió.
es.R: Entonces Dios hizo la cúpula. Separó el agua que estaba debajo de la cúpula del agua que estaba encima. Y eso fue lo que pasó.

fr.L: Et Dieu fit la voûte, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} sépara entre les eaux qui [étaient] au-dessous de la voûte et les eaux qui [étaient] au-dessus de la voûte. Et ce fut ainsi.
fr.B: Dieu fit donc la voûte et sépara les eaux qui se trouvaient au-dessous d’elle de celles qui se trouvaient au-dessus. Et il en alla ainsi.
fr.R: Alors Dieu a fait le dôme. Il a séparé l’eau qui était sous le dôme de l’eau qui était au-dessus. Et c’est ce qui s’est passé.

sw.L: Na Mungu akalifanya kuba, akatenganisha kati ya maji ambayo [yalikuwa] chini ya kuba na maji ambayo [yalikuwa] juu ya kuba. Na ikawa hivyo.
sw.B: Basi Mungu akalifanya kuba, akayatenganisha maji yaliyokuwa chini yake na maji yaliyokuwa juu yake. Ndivyo ilivyokuwa.
sw.R: Basi Mungu akatengeneza kuba hilo. Akatenganisha maji yaliyokuwa chini ya kuba na maji yaliyokuwa juu yake. Na hivyo ndivyo ilivyotokea.

decisions.choice: the waters above the vault: water held back above the sky
decisions.reason: The account pictures water both below the vault and above it. When the flood comes, "the windows of the heavens" are opened (7:11), and Psalm 148:4 calls on "the waters above the heavens" to praise God.

decisions.choice: and it was so: what God commanded happened, exactly as he said
decisions.reason: This short report follows six of God's commands in the chapter (verses 7, 9, 11, 15, 24, 30). It confirms that his word was carried out as he spoke it.

decisions.choice: and it was so at the end of verse 7, as in the Hebrew text
alternatives: and it was so at the end of verse 6 (Septuagint)
decisions.reason: Elsewhere in the chapter "and it was so" comes straight after God's command. Here the Hebrew text places it after the report of what God made; the Greek Septuagint has it at the end of verse 6 instead, in the usual place. The Hebrew, the less expected order, is followed here.

decisions.choice: And so it happened (B); And that is what happened (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew "and it was so". Balanced and Readable say the same in current English.

source.text: וַיִּקְרָ֧א אֱלֹהִ֛ים לָֽרָקִ֖יעַ שָׁמָ֑יִם וַֽיְהִי־עֶ֥רֶב וַֽיְהִי־בֹ֖קֶר י֥וֹם שֵׁנִֽי׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And called God to the vault heavens. And was evening and was morning, day second.

en.L: And God called the vault Heavens. And there was evening and there was morning, a second day.
en.B: God named the vault Sky. Evening came, and then morning: the second day.
en.R: God gave the dome the name Sky. Evening passed, and morning came. That was the second day.

es.L: Y llamó Dios a la bóveda Cielos. Y hubo tarde y hubo mañana, un segundo día.
es.B: Dios dio a la bóveda el nombre de Cielo. Llegó la tarde, y después la mañana: el segundo día.
es.R: Dios le puso a la cúpula el nombre de Cielo. Pasó la tarde y llegó la mañana. Ese fue el segundo día.

fr.L: Et Dieu appela la voûte Cieux. Et il y eut un soir et il y eut un matin, un deuxième jour.
fr.B: Dieu nomma la voûte Ciel. Le soir vint, puis le matin : le deuxième jour.
fr.R: Dieu a donné au dôme le nom de Ciel. Le soir est passé, puis le matin est venu. C’était le deuxième jour.

sw.L: Na Mungu akaliita kuba Mbingu. Na kukawa jioni, na kukawa asubuhi, siku ya pili.
sw.B: Mungu akalipa kuba jina Anga. Jioni ikaja, kisha asubuhi: siku ya pili.
sw.R: Mungu akalipa kuba jina la Anga. Jioni ikapita, asubuhi ikafika. Hiyo ilikuwa siku ya pili.

decisions.choice: heavens: here the visible sky, the vault overhead
decisions.reason: This is the word of verse 1. Here it is the name God gives the vault: the sky above the earth, where the birds fly (verse 20) and the lights are set (verse 14). Elsewhere it can also mean the place where God dwells (1 Kings 8:30).

decisions.choice: no "God saw that it was good" on the second day, as in the Hebrew text
alternatives: And God saw that it was good (Septuagint)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text has no verdict "good" on the second day; the Greek Septuagint adds it here, as on the other days. The Hebrew is followed. The work of separating the waters begun on day two is finished on day three, which has the verdict twice (verses 10 and 12).

decisions.choice: Sky
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "Heavens", the word of verse 1. Balanced and Readable say "Sky", because that is what the vault is (m1), and "heaven" alone suggests to most readers the dwelling of God.

decisions.choice: Cielo
decisions.reason: Spanish has one word, "cielo", for both the sky and heaven. Literal keeps the plural "Cielos", the word of verse 1; Balanced and Readable use the singular, the everyday word for the sky, which is what the vault is (m1).

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֗ים יִקָּו֨וּ הַמַּ֜יִם מִתַּ֤חַת הַשָּׁמַ֨יִם֙ אֶל־מָק֣וֹם אֶחָ֔ד וְתֵרָאֶ֖ה הַיַּבָּשָׁ֑ה וַֽיְהִי־כֵֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And said God, let be gathered the waters from under the heavens to place one, and let appear the dry [land]. And was so.

en.L: And God said, "Let the waters under the heavens be gathered to one place, and let the dry [land] appear." And it was so.
en.B: Then God said, "Let the waters below the sky come together into one place, and let dry land be seen." And so it happened.
en.R: Then God said, "Let the water under the sky come together in one place, so that dry land appears." And that is what happened.

es.L: Y dijo Dios: «Reúnanse las aguas de debajo de los cielos en un lugar, y aparezca lo seco». Y fue así.
es.B: Entonces Dios dijo: «Que las aguas que están bajo el cielo se junten en un solo lugar, y que se vea la tierra seca». Y así sucedió.
es.R: Entonces Dios dijo: «Que el agua que está debajo del cielo se junte en un lugar, para que aparezca la tierra seca». Y eso fue lo que pasó.

fr.L: Et Dieu dit : « Que les eaux de dessous les cieux soient rassemblées en un seul lieu, et que la [terre] sèche apparaisse. » Et ce fut ainsi.
fr.B: Puis Dieu dit : « Que les eaux qui sont sous le ciel se réunissent en un même endroit, et que la terre ferme se montre ! » Et il en alla ainsi.
fr.R: Puis Dieu a dit : « Que l’eau qui est sous le ciel se rassemble à un seul endroit, pour qu’on voie apparaître la terre sèche. » Et c’est ce qui s’est passé.

sw.L: Na Mungu akasema, "Maji ya chini ya mbingu yakusanywe mahali pamoja, na pakavu paonekane." Na ikawa hivyo.
sw.B: Kisha Mungu akasema, "Maji yaliyo chini ya anga yakutane mahali pamoja, na ardhi kavu ionekane." Ndivyo ilivyokuwa.
sw.R: Kisha Mungu akasema, "Maji yaliyo chini ya anga yakusanyike sehemu moja, ili nchi kavu itokee." Na hivyo ndivyo ilivyotokea.

decisions.choice: the dry land: ground no longer covered by water
decisions.reason: The word means simply "the dry": ground from which the water has gone. The same word is used when Israel crosses the sea "on dry ground" (Exodus 14:16), one of several echoes of this chapter in the story of the exodus.

decisions.choice: the Hebrew text has no report that the waters were gathered
alternatives: a further sentence: and the water was gathered into its gatherings, and the dry land appeared (Septuagint)
decisions.reason: The Greek Septuagint adds a sentence telling how the waters were gathered and the dry land appeared, as the account does after other commands. The Hebrew text does not have it and is followed here.

decisions.choice: the dry [land]
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the dry"; Literal brackets the noun English needs.

decisions.choice: lo seco
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the dry". Spanish can make a noun of the adjective with "lo", so Literal needs no bracketed word here.

decisions.choice: pakavu
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says simply "the dry" (m1). Swahili can say it in one word with the place prefix, "pakavu" (a dry place), so Literal needs no bracketed noun; Balanced and Readable say "ardhi kavu", "nchi kavu".

source.text: וַיִּקְרָ֨א אֱלֹהִ֤ים׀לַיַּבָּשָׁה֙ אֶ֔רֶץ וּלְמִקְוֵ֥ה הַמַּ֖יִם קָרָ֣א יַמִּ֑ים וַיַּ֥רְא אֱלֹהִ֖ים כִּי־טֽוֹב׃

records.literal_gloss: And called God to the dry [land] earth, and to the gathering of the waters he called seas. And saw God that [it was] good.

en.L: And God called the dry [land] Earth, and the gathering of the waters {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called Seas. And God saw that [it was] good.
en.B: God named the dry land Earth, and the gathered waters {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} named Seas. And God saw that it was good.
en.R: God gave the dry land the name Earth, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave the water that had come together the name Seas. God saw that it was good.

es.L: Y llamó Dios a lo seco Tierra, y a la reunión de las aguas llamó Mares. Y vio Dios que [era] bueno.
es.B: Dios dio a la tierra seca el nombre de Tierra, y a las aguas reunidas, el de Mares. Y Dios vio que era bueno.
es.R: Dios le puso a la tierra seca el nombre de Tierra, y al agua que se había juntado le puso el nombre de Mares. Dios vio que era bueno.

fr.L: Et Dieu appela la [terre] sèche Terre, et le rassemblement des eaux, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} l’appela Mers. Et Dieu vit que [c’était] bon.
fr.B: Dieu nomma la terre ferme Terre, et les eaux rassemblées, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les nomma Mers. Et Dieu vit que c’était bon.
fr.R: Dieu a donné à la terre sèche le nom de Terre, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a donné à l’eau rassemblée le nom de Mers. Dieu a vu que c’était bon.

sw.L: Na Mungu akapaita pakavu Nchi, na makusanyiko ya maji akayaita Bahari. Na Mungu akaona kwamba [ni] vyema.
sw.B: Mungu akaipa ardhi kavu jina Nchi, na maji yaliyokusanyika akayapa jina Bahari. Mungu akaona kwamba ni vyema.
sw.R: Mungu akaipa nchi kavu jina la Nchi, na maji yaliyokusanyika pamoja akayapa jina la Bahari. Mungu akaona kwamba ni vizuri.

decisions.choice: earth: here the land, as against the seas
decisions.reason: The word that meant the whole earth in verses 1 and 2 is here the name of the dry land. It can also mean a single country, as in "the land of Egypt" (Exodus 7:19).

decisions.choice: seas: all the gathered waters, not one particular sea
decisions.reason: The plural takes in every body of water: the "one place" of verse 9, seen as many seas.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֗ים תַּֽדְשֵׁ֤א הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ דֶּ֔שֶׁא עֵ֚שֶׂב מַזְרִ֣יעַ זֶ֔רַע עֵ֣ץ פְּרִ֞י עֹ֤שֶׂה פְּרִי֙ לְמִינ֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר זַרְעוֹ־ב֖וֹ עַל־הָאָ֑רֶץ וַֽיְהִי־כֵֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And said God, let sprout the earth vegetation, plant[s] seeding seed, tree[s] of fruit making fruit to its kind, which its seed [is] in it, on the earth. And was so.

en.L: And God said, "Let the earth sprout vegetation: plants yielding seed, [and] fruit trees bearing fruit according to its kind, with its seed in it, on the earth." And it was so.
en.B: Then God said, "Let the earth put forth green growth: plants that produce seed, and trees on the earth that bear fruit with its seed inside, each according to its kind." And so it happened.
en.R: Then God said, "Let plants grow on the land: plants that make seeds, and trees with fruit that has seeds in it, each of its own kind." And that is what happened.

es.L: Y dijo Dios: «Haga brotar la tierra vegetación: plantas que den semilla, [y] árboles frutales que den fruto según su especie, con su semilla en él, sobre la tierra». Y fue así.
es.B: Entonces Dios dijo: «Que la tierra se cubra de verdor: plantas que produzcan semilla, y árboles sobre la tierra que den fruto con su semilla dentro, cada uno según su especie». Y así sucedió.
es.R: Entonces Dios dijo: «Que crezcan plantas en la tierra: plantas que den semillas, y árboles con frutos que tengan semillas dentro, cada uno de su propia especie». Y eso fue lo que pasó.

fr.L: Et Dieu dit : « Que la terre fasse germer de la verdure : des plantes produisant de la semence, [et] des arbres à fruit portant du fruit selon leur espèce, avec sa semence en lui, sur la terre. » Et ce fut ainsi.
fr.B: Puis Dieu dit : « Que la terre fasse pousser de la verdure : des plantes qui donnent de la semence, et des arbres qui, sur la terre, portent des fruits avec leur semence à l’intérieur, chacun selon son espèce. » Et il en alla ainsi.
fr.R: Puis Dieu a dit : « Que des plantes poussent sur la terre : des plantes qui font des graines, et des arbres avec des fruits qui ont des graines à l’intérieur, chacun selon sa sorte. » Et c’est ce qui s’est passé.

sw.L: Na Mungu akasema, "Nchi na ichipushe uoto: mimea itoayo mbegu, [na] miti ya matunda izaayo matunda kulingana na aina yake, yenye mbegu yake ndani yake, juu ya nchi." Na ikawa hivyo.
sw.B: Kisha Mungu akasema, "Nchi itoe mimea ya kijani: mimea inayozaa mbegu, na miti juu ya nchi inayozaa matunda yenye mbegu ndani yake, kila mmea na kila mti kulingana na aina yake." Ndivyo ilivyokuwa.
sw.R: Kisha Mungu akasema, "Mimea iote juu ya nchi: mimea inayotoa mbegu, na miti yenye matunda yaliyo na mbegu ndani yake, kila mmea na kila mti kwa aina yake." Na hivyo ndivyo ilivyotokea.

decisions.choice: let the earth sprout: the earth brings forth at God's command
decisions.reason: God speaks to the earth, and it brings forth (verse 12), as the waters do in verse 20 and the earth again in verse 24. The power is in God's word; the earth is the means.

decisions.choice: vegetation, plants and trees: green growth in general, then its two main kinds
decisions.reason: The first word covers all fresh green growth. The two that follow name its main kinds as they are seen: plants that carry their seed openly, such as grain and herbs, and trees whose seed is inside the fruit. This is a description of what is seen, not a full botany.

decisions.choice: according to its kind: each kind producing more of its own kind
decisions.reason: The phrase comes ten times in the chapter (verses 11, 12, 21, 24, 25). Each kind of plant and animal reproduces its own kind through its seed, so that the life God has made goes on from generation to generation. The Hebrew word for kind is not a modern scientific category such as species.

decisions.choice: [and] fruit trees
decisions.reason: The Hebrew lists the kinds without "and"; Literal brackets the one English needs.

decisions.choice: según su especie
decisions.reason: "Especie" is the established word in this formula, and in everyday Spanish it still means a kind or sort ("una especie de"), not only a species of biology; as m3 says, the Hebrew word is not a scientific category. "Género", the older rendering, now sounds technical or grammatical; "clase" and "tipo" are plainer but weaker in a phrase repeated ten times in the chapter. The same word is used at every level.

decisions.choice: selon leur espèce (L); chacun selon son espèce (B); chacun selon sa sorte (R)
alternatives: selon leur espèce at every level
decisions.reason: "Selon son espèce" is the usual French for this phrase, and it is kept at Literal and Balanced; the word is not meant as the modern scientific category (m3). Readable says "sorte", the everyday word, so that young readers do not hear a biology term.

decisions.choice: uoto (L), mimea ya kijani (B); kulingana na aina yake (L, B), kwa aina yake (R)
decisions.reason: "Uoto" is the general word for vegetation, the first and widest of the three terms (m2); "majani" suggests grass or leaves. "Aina" is the ordinary word for a kind or sort, not a scientific species (m3).

source.text: וַתּוֹצֵ֨א הָאָ֜רֶץ דֶּ֠שֶׁא עֵ֣שֶׂב מַזְרִ֤יעַ זֶ֨רַע֙ לְמִינֵ֔הוּ וְעֵ֧ץ עֹֽשֶׂה־פְּרִ֛יאֲשֶׁ֥ר זַרְעוֹ־ב֖וֹ לְמִינֵ֑הוּ וַיַּ֥רְא אֱלֹהִ֖ים כִּי־טֽוֹב׃

records.literal_gloss: And brought forth the earth vegetation, plant[s] seeding seed to its kind, and tree[s] making fruit which its seed [is] in it to its kind. And saw God that [it was] good.

en.L: And the earth brought forth vegetation, plants yielding seed according to their kind, and trees bearing fruit with its seed in it according to their kind. And God saw that [it was] good.
en.B: The earth brought forth green growth: plants that produce seed, each according to its kind, and trees that bear fruit with its seed inside, each according to its kind. And God saw that it was good.
en.R: So the land grew plants that made seeds, and trees with fruit that had seeds in it, each of its own kind. God saw that it was good.

es.L: Y produjo la tierra vegetación, plantas que dan semilla según su especie, y árboles que dan fruto con su semilla en él según su especie. Y vio Dios que [era] bueno.
es.B: La tierra produjo verdor: plantas que dan semilla, cada una según su especie, y árboles que dan fruto con su semilla dentro, cada uno según su especie. Y Dios vio que era bueno.
es.R: Así, en la tierra crecieron plantas que daban semillas, y árboles con frutos que tenían semillas dentro, cada uno de su propia especie. Dios vio que era bueno.

fr.L: Et la terre fit sortir de la verdure, des plantes produisant de la semence selon leur espèce, et des arbres portant du fruit avec sa semence en lui selon leur espèce. Et Dieu vit que [c’était] bon.
fr.B: La terre produisit de la verdure : des plantes qui donnent de la semence, chacune selon son espèce, et des arbres qui portent des fruits avec leur semence à l’intérieur, chacun selon son espèce. Et Dieu vit que c’était bon.
fr.R: Alors des plantes ont poussé sur la terre, des plantes qui faisaient des graines, et des arbres avec des fruits qui avaient des graines à l’intérieur, chacun selon sa sorte. Dieu a vu que c’était bon.

sw.L: Na nchi ikatoa uoto, mimea itoayo mbegu kulingana na aina yake, na miti izaayo matunda yenye mbegu yake ndani yake kulingana na aina yake. Na Mungu akaona kwamba [ni] vyema.
sw.B: Nchi ikatoa mimea ya kijani: mimea inayozaa mbegu, kila mmea kulingana na aina yake, na miti inayozaa matunda yenye mbegu ndani yake, kila mti kulingana na aina yake. Mungu akaona kwamba ni vyema.
sw.R: Basi mimea ikaota juu ya nchi, mimea iliyotoa mbegu, na miti yenye matunda yaliyokuwa na mbegu ndani yake, kila mmea na kila mti kwa aina yake. Mungu akaona kwamba ni vizuri.

decisions.choice: the earth brought forth: the report repeats the command
decisions.reason: The report repeats God's command in almost the same words, with "brought forth" for "sprout". The trees are no longer said to be "on the earth", and "according to its kind" is now said of the plants as well.

decisions.choice: according to their kind
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "its kind", of each plant and tree; Literal says "their", since English refers to "plants" and "trees" in the plural.

records.literal_gloss: And was evening and was morning, day third.

en.L: And there was evening and there was morning, a third day.
en.B: Evening came, and then morning: the third day.
en.R: Evening passed, and morning came. That was the third day.

es.L: Y hubo tarde y hubo mañana, un tercer día.
es.B: Llegó la tarde, y después la mañana: el tercer día.
es.R: Pasó la tarde y llegó la mañana. Ese fue el tercer día.

fr.L: Et il y eut un soir et il y eut un matin, un troisième jour.
fr.B: Le soir vint, puis le matin : le troisième jour.
fr.R: Le soir est passé, puis le matin est venu. C’était le troisième jour.

sw.L: Na kukawa jioni, na kukawa asubuhi, siku ya tatu.
sw.B: Jioni ikaja, kisha asubuhi: siku ya tatu.
sw.R: Jioni ikapita, asubuhi ikafika. Hiyo ilikuwa siku ya tatu.
